findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() will not compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method with that name, added in `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160), takes a `UserModel` parameter. No zero-argument overload exists in the class hierarchy, so this is a compilation error and the services module will not build. It should probably be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, or a dedicated no-arg helper.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are dropped from the normal login page
findings.body:
Previously the conditional-UI webauthn data was filled when no user was selected yet (the normal first-login case). The new helper returns true only when `user != null`. Both `authenticate` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) now skip `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm` on the initial username/password page. They also skip it on error pages after a failed login, because `getUser` clears the context user before the error challenge.

Result: discoverable-passkey and conditional-UI login no longer work for regular (non re-authentication) logins. The new tests on initial login (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithExternalKey`) expect the `webauth` form there. The fix was meant to also enable passkeys when a user is set, not only then; the `user != null` clause should be removed.
